result.text: Continuing פרק י, chapter 10, we're in the middle, down near the bottom of the first page, and that's ק"ט, say, עמוד ב. So we've last time talked about the light before the צמצום and how we need to understand the idea of how we can talk about ספירות there, seemingly it's completely simple and beyond any sort of description, how can we talk about it, and yet, on the other hand, we say that we're supposed to study even there in a detailed way. And like we find, again, in רמב"ם and other sources where we do talk about our concept of God, basically God Himself, and what it means His transcendent existence that's higher than creation, what that is like. So what does that look like from the perspective of חסידות and explaining these ideas that are found in קבלה and חקירה and different Jewish sources. Okay, so now we're going to give some analogies to help us understand this: והדמיון בזה ידוע, and the metaphor, the comparison that we make to this is known, מכחות הנפש, from the human soul, we compare it to our soul and our soul's different faculties, בהתגלות מרצון עד המעשה, when our different faculties are revealed, we have 10 faculties starting from רצון, and then we have חכמה, בינה, all these different corresponding 10 faculties all the way down to the faculty of action, שישנם כולם בפרט בהעלם אור עצמות הנפש שנקרא בחינת יחידה, and all of these exist first in a hidden way within the light of the essence of the soul, which is called יחידה. And so this relationship between the essence of our soul, the יחידה, to the various כחות, that is a metaphor, that is a comparison to understand this relationship of a completely simple essence to what comes after it, which is the משל we're going to use to help us understand God's simple essence and how that relates to the 10 ספירות. And the basic idea, this is something that the אלטר רבי talks about elsewhere and in, you know, many other places, that the essence of our soul is something that even we don't know, that we feel that we're alive, we feel that we have this soul, but its essence is something that transcends our understanding, and it transcends any particular form, even that we could describe to ourselves, and yet we see that we, our essence is expressed in all sorts of different ways. So that's the basic idea that we're going to talk about. כמו על דרך דוגמא, for example, כאשר אדם הוא חפץ חסד וטוב להיטיב בדבר פרט, let's say somebody is, right, he's a kind person and he desires to actually help somebody in a particular way. By the way, when the difference between the word חסד and טוב in Hebrew, חסד means kindness, which is more a feeling within a person, and טוב means to do good, to actually benefit somebody else. So it's more one is more focused on your feeling and your desire and one is more the idea of the action that's and the result that's actually benefiting somebody else. But either way, a person wants to do kindness to help somebody in some particular way, שזהו בא מצד שיש בו מדה זו שחפץ חסד וטוב בבחינת עצמות נפשו הנקרא יחידה, what is the source of that motivation, why is the person doing this kindness, why is he helping this person, it's because within the essence of the human soul, one of the characteristics that God endowed with us is this essential nature of kindness and empathy and a desire to help other people and to contribute and and, you know, all of those things. So על כן בא חפץ חסד זה בגילוי מן ההעלם, and so therefore this essential desire of kindness is now being revealed and being expressed when the person comes to a situation where that's necessary. So here we have this interesting relationship where when the person is just sitting at home, they didn't have any particular desire to help this person. And what we're trying to explain here is this relationship of an essence, an essence to its revelation. And so an essence is by nature something that's transcendent, and like we talked about in קונטרס ענינה של תורת החסידות, where we compare this idea of the יחידה in חסידות and an essence to oil, and we said basically there's three characteristics of it, one is that it's the essence and therefore it's found in everything, and that's why we find from, you know, humans to animals to plants to even inanimate things, they all have some form of oil, so that's an analogy for this idea of something that's an essence is that it's found in everything, and it's kind of like the distilled, concentrated energy, that's that's what oil and fat is, it's like storing up the energy, so maybe in that sense also it's related to the idea of an essence in a physical way, and oil floats on top of everything, and it permeates everything. And so this is the idea that the relationship of an essence is something that it's the essence of everything, and it transcends any of the particular forms or details, but then it's also found within all of the particulars. So this is the idea we find here with this desire for kindness. So in other words, the essential desire to help people and to be kind doesn't relate to any particular detail. When a person's just sitting there, they didn't want to, you know, help some old lady across the street or give money to a particular organization or do any of those things. Those are all circumstantial, they're based on the circumstances that the person finds themselves in. But in any situation, based on their understanding and evaluation of that situation, if they see that the person needs help, if a person needs, you know, he needs coats, he needs shoes, he needs food, whatever it is that the person needs, a kind person is going to then be motivated to help the person in that particular way. So we see that that the essential desire really stays something that transcends and is abstract, that's beyond any of these particular details, but then it motivates and gives rise to all these particulars based on the situation in the world around them. And so we have this relationship of the essential desire of kindness within the person is this abstract essence that doesn't, so to speak, relate to or know about the details of the world or even kind of care about the details of the world. But then, when the person looks around into the world, and like we talked about this a little bit in ר' הלל's ביאור, this idea of like looking at something and having those ניצוצות, those sparks come back and arouse a desire, that's the idea. When a person, they have this innate thing they're looking for of opportunities to do kindness, and they're sitting there like אברהם was sitting at the gate of his tent, he was looking for an opportunity to do kindness, when he saw a situation come up, then that wakes up this desire, and then it gets manifest in a particular way. He saw the three guests coming, he went and he had them wash their feet, and sit under a tree to cool down, and gave them food and drink and things like that, and was manifest in a particular way based on the needs of the situation. So that's the basic idea that we're of this משל. ומוכרח לומר, and so we must say, בודאי, with certainty, שחפץ חסד זה בעצמות נפשו הוא בבחינת כח היולי, that this essential desire of kindness, the way it's in the essence of the soul, is what is described as a as a כח היולי. The word היולי is translated in Yiddish as essence, so this is, you know, coming from, you know, possibly a Greek word, but it means the idea of something that's a completely essential thing that doesn't have any defined form. בעצמיות, within the essence, לכלול כל מה שעתיד לחפוץ בחסד וטוב, and it includes within itself the potential or like the יכולת, the ability to generate whatever a person's ever destined to desire in terms of kindness and goodness. בכל פרטי פרטי ענינים שיבקשו ממנו, with all the minute details of whatever will be required requested from him, he's going to be able to generate the desire to do those things. ואם כן בהכרח שקודם שעלה ברצונו וחפצו זה בגילוי להיטיב חסדו בדבר זה הפרטי, so before, you know, the guests came to אברהם or anything like that where there was no particular manifestation for how this essential desire is going to be expressed, it's just an innate quality within the soul, so before those details came up, היה כלול בעצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי, so these the possibility of that happening was just included within their essential desire for kindness, this this היולי desire for kindness, ויצא מן ההיולי להתגלות בדבר פרטי זה, and then, when the situation arose, this essential desire for kindness, which is totally abstract and doesn't doesn't really relate to any particular detail, now in the situation it got plugged into that situation and it became manifest in this particular way of giving the people food, for example, or whatever, you know, any situation needs. And you see this, a person that's a kind person, they're always expressing that in different ways whenever there's a situation that they can help, whether it's a it's a child, whether it's an adult, whether whatever it is, they're going to find a way to help somebody in in so many different ways. And we see this also, you know, even with the רבי or things like that, you know, sometimes it would be giving somebody a reference to a doctor or this or, you know, sometimes it's a blessing, sometimes it's a spiritual thing, sometimes it's a physical thing, whatever you could do to help the person, it's always going to come out according to the needs of that individual and the time and situation. ואנו רואים שיש בחפץ חסד זה שכל וחכמה ומדות ומחשבה דבור ומעשה, and we see that when this desire for kindness is manifest, it in order to effectively help somebody, you need to have שכל, you have to have intellect, you have to understand the situation, evaluate what do they really need, what's really going to help them, and you have to do it with, you know, with wisdom, and there's emotions involved, how you feel about, based on the situation, you feel about what's good for them, bad for them. If a person's sick, for example, and they need certain medications, and certain types of foods are good for them, certain things are bad for them, so that's going to give you these emotions of wanting to get them what they need and keep them away from what's not good for them, things like that. But it's obviously all according to the situation. You could have one person that a certain medication is lifesaving, and for another person that same thing would be, you know, very dangerous, and and so the the feelings about the how these things relate to the person and the situation is very different, the The same thing, you know, if you want to help somebody that, you know, is really poor and they need a loan, and it's really going to help them, so you'll desire to give them money. If on the other hand, if a person is, let's say, spoiled and they just want money, but they're going to squander it and just, you know, spend it on gambling and drinking and things like that, so then kindness is actually going to say, no, I'm enabling that, I'm not going to give it to them, I'm going to try to, you know, get them to learn to work and to be responsible and things like that. So your feelings of חסד and גבורה towards the same actions are going to change, and that requires understanding, and then that generates מדות, and based on that, it generates מחשבה דיבור ומעשה, a certain way of thinking, a certain way of talking, and a certain way of acting. And again, this the same desire of kindness could even generate an external type of speech that might be harsh or strict, but it's really for the kindness, like when you love a child, you're going to sometimes discipline them. And but that's really coming from a love for them and a desire to teach them to have good manners and good מדות and to be, you know, kind and tolerant and flexible and things like that. אם כן, so if so, that we see that on the one hand this desire within the essence was completely a simple abstract thing that didn't relate to any of these details, didn't contain within it any knowledge or thought of the outside world, it's just something that has to do with yourself. And this is the main distinction when we're speaking about, you know, the levels like before the סדר השתלשלות, before the צמצום I mean, and even, you know, really until we get into like אצילות, that a lot of times the משל for this is the way things are with internally within the person, in other words, if you look inside of yourself, you have a certain nature and certain desires and certain preferences. But then there's the way those plug into the outside world, and that comes from looking, one comes from looking in and one comes from looking out. And so these are very different type of things in their nature, and the things that are on internal to a person are more essential and they're more abstract, and then the way they become expressed on the outside is based on the world and those are more concrete. And so that's the basic idea that we're looking at here. There's the internal desire for kindness that because God gave us a human soul that we have this essential quality of empathy, this essential ability and desire and need to be kind and empathetic and help people and things like that. But that essential desire doesn't have any direct connection to anything in the world. It's totally abstract, it's an abstract essence. But then it has the ability to motivate and generate all kinds of particular desires and motivate different ways of thinking and feeling and acting and everything like that, based on our evaluation of the situation, how we plug that into the situation. So אם כן ודאי במקור חפץ חסד זה בהעלמו, כשהיה כלול בעצמיות החפץ חסד ההיולי. So here again, we're seeing these two sides, the side, so here again, we're seeing the two sides: the side that is essential and abstract, and we can't describe or define in terms of the world, and that is when we look at the way this kindness was when it was hidden within the person's essential desire of kindness, the היולי desire of kindness. So at that point, it doesn't have any of these divisions of שכל and מדות and any of these kind of things. But yet, we can kind of ascribe, as as speak about what came afterwards, since we see that it actually motivated this particular desire with this way of thinking, we can say that they came from there. And so we can kind of, you know, attribute these to their source. So therefore, גם כן מהתחלקות שכל ומדות מחשבה דיבור ומעשה שבו, so this essential source, we can say, also was the source of all these different divisions of the intellect and the emotions and the thoughts, speech, and action that came out with this kindness. אבל בבחינת עצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי כמו שהוא קודם שבא עדיין בדבר פרטי. But when we're speaking about, so we can think about this desire within the person in two ways: the way that it actually got plugged into a particular desire, at which point we can kind of attribute the these different aspects to it and say, well, it was the source of these things. But then we can also think about this essential desire for kindness the way it was before it got plugged into any particular desire or kindness, and at that point, and again, we're thinking about the same thing, nothing is changing as far as the essence, it's just the way that we think about it and how we talk about it. So when we think about it in terms of how it is essentially before it got plugged into this situation, and in theory it could have never happened and then it wouldn't have actually arose and and brought about this situation. So at that point, before it came בדבר פרטי, הגם שבודאי גם שם יש התחלקות שכל ומדות וכולי. So even there, we must say that it had the possibility to generate all these different details of the intellect and emotions, etc. מכל מקום כולם מתאחדים בתכלית, but at that point, when we're looking at it from that perspective, they're all really one. There's just the essential power of kindness, this essential nature within the person, מתאחדים בתכלית, and so we can't really speak of any division. And so this is the basic metaphor that we're talking about. So we can, this, we have this essential desire of kindness. This essential desire then gets plugged into details later outside in the world, and so we can look at it in terms of, from the perspective of once it gets plugged in, or we can look at it from the perspective of before it's plugged in. And when we, in one, from one side, we'll speak of it as relating to the details that came afterwards, and from the other side, we'll say, no, really it transcends those details, and all those specifics are just essentially the same thing. Because from that point of view, you just, you want to do whatever's kindness. It doesn't matter if it's this way or that way, you don't really care. And like a lot of times, you'll see let's say, you know, two mature adults can have a discussion about what's, how to go about accomplishing something. They both want the same general thing, and they could have many strategies, and it really is irrelevant in the end if you do it this way or that way. You know, they both can work, and so they could agree to go either way. וכמו כן במידה פרטית אחרת שבעצמיות, and the same general relationship applies to any of the other particular attributes the way they're in the essence, כמו מידת הגבורה והתפארת והנצח וכהאי גוונא. So we have an essential attribute of justice that we want things to be, you know, to be just and things like that. So that's an essential attribute that God gives us, and therefore that's going to make us want to have rules and to, you know, punish the wicked and things like that. So that essential attribute of גבורה also can motivate all sorts of different things, and we have this similar type of relationship. The same thing with the essential idea of תפארת, of seeking beauty, wanting to beautify things, wanting to praise and and, you know, show off beautiful things that we that we appreciate, that essential attribute. And again, you know, it can be expressed in a good way, in a bad way. It could be a person showing off in a negative way, or it could be wanting to beautify things like the תורה and stuff like that. It's all coming from this the same essential desire. The question is how it gets plugged in. Does it get plugged into something good, does it get plugged into something bad? That's that's a separate thing we'll talk about later. והנצח, and the same thing, the desire to overcome challenges and win. So, you know, a person that likes challenges is going to love all sorts of puzzles and all sorts of games and competition and things like that. And, you know, and whether it's in a fun way or whether it's in a serious way of overcoming an opponent in battle or whatever it is, that essential desire that God gives us to want to dominate and to want to win and to want to overcome a challenge can be expressed in, you know, millions of ways. And when it gets plugged into one situation, right, a person might become very into chess, or they might be into wrestling, or they might be fighting a war, or whatever it is, or it could be just within their personal struggles trying to overcome the יצר הרע and things like that. All these situations, a person could be plugging in this essential attribute of נצח. And again, the essence of it transcends any of those details, but then when it gets plugged in, it takes on and becomes the source of and and motivation for all those details. וכהאי גוונא, and so too with the other attributes. עד בחינת המלכות, and this is true even of מלכות, שהוא מידת התנשאות, which you might maybe I think maybe he specifies מלכות because you might think that מלכות essentially relates to others, it's like the idea of, you know, being a king and being over other people, but that also has this type of relationship, שכולו בוודאי מיוחד רצון וחפץ למלוך וחכמה ומידות ומחשבה וכו'. And so, so too, this essential attribute of מלכות is that God puts within a person this essential nature to, you know, rule over things, to dominate things, and it's expressed, we see even, like it says, little kids will dominate animals and things like that and kind of rule over them, but that's like an immature expression of it. And then there's this deeper thing of leadership that comes out, and usually it's not going to come out unless there's a situation where people need them to lead and they request from the person to lead, and and they accept the person's leadership, and then a person will this essential quality of leadership, which, again, a person has and it might be dormant, but when that situation comes up where they need to lead and they see that they can do it, it will come out. And, you know, part of this even comes out as being a parent. You have to be a leader within your own home, and even a person doesn't feel that, you know, beforehand, but when you feel responsible for others, it brings out this this sense that, you know, you have this superiority, you understand more than your kids and therefore you're responsible for them, and it brings out this deep sense of leadership, which generates all sorts of, again, desires and ways of thinking and emotions that are natural and relate to that particular desire, and a certain way of thinking and talking and acting and everything that relates to that. So with all these מידות, we have this type of relationship. אך קודם שבא לבחינת התגלות בדבר פרט, כמו למלוך על מדינה זו וכהאי גוונא, but, for example, with this attribute of kingship, before it came and was plugged into a particular thing like to be a king over a particular nation, so, you know, let's say you have baby Napoleon or, you know, whatever it is, before he didn't know where what country he was in, it didn't relate to that in any particular way, וכאי גוונא כלולים ומיוחדים בתכלית בבחינת מידת המלוכה ההיולית העצמית, so all of the details of what it means to be a leader and a king were just included in this essential nature within the the soul, that the soul has this essential ability to of kingship and leadership, and it didn't relate to making any particular type of policies and politics or anything like that. כמו בעצמות חפץ חסד ההיולי הנ"ל, just the same way with the essential desire for kindness. Just like there all the details of the kindness didn't exist yet within the self, so too all the details of the attribute of kingship didn't exist yet there, they come out based on the situation. ואם כן, if so, מובן ממילא, it's understood, שבבחינת now we're generalizing that just like we see that this is true with each of these attributes and how they relate to they're the essence of all the details that come out from them, so too the essence of the soul is like this type of essence that includes all these 10 attributes, and all these 10 attributes are really just different ways that this the the one essence of the soul is expressed. ואם כן מובן ממילא, it's automatically understood, שבבחינת מידות העצמיות דכתר, חכמה, בינה, וחסד, גבורה, תפארת, נצח, הוד, יסוד, מלכות ההיוליים שבעצמיות הנפש, לא ייתכן לומר גם לשון זה שמתאחדים וכלולים בעצמיות הנפש הנקרא יחידה. You can't describe these essential attributes as being something separate from the essence, from the יחידה, that is then united with them. And like we talked about again in קונטרס ענינה של תורת החסידות, that the relationship of the יחידה, of the essence of the soul, to all of the different faculties and attributes that come out from it is not that it is a source that unites them and includes them, but rather it's something that completely transcends those details, it's a completely higher essence which automatically gives rise to all of them. And so this is the relationship we're talking about here, that the יחידה, that God gives us this essence that we have this essential nature, this ability to to have choice and to express ourselves, and this is kind of in an essential, unlimited way. Now our in the משל, it's a little different than the נמשל because the human soul does get imprinted with a certain form like we talked about in רב הלל's ביאור, and actually it's a process that starts out completely simple and then that spark becomes somewhat defined. But even at this point where it's, you know, somewhat defined, to the essence of the soul there's no real difference between this idea of חסד or גבורה or מלכות or any of these things. It's just that the essence can choose to express itself and be itself, and it has this unlimited ability and freedom to choose and to express itself and to be itself, and it's just coming out in all these different ways. And so you we can't speak of of them as really being separate things that are like attaching to the soul or that are separate from the soul, it's really just the soul itself. And that the differences that we talk about only arise once the soul expresses itself in the world, then it takes on these different forms, and therefore we speak about them as being separate. But from the point of view of the essence, it's really the same power that's just plugging into and turning on all these different attributes. מאחר, so we can't speak of them as being separate from the essence, מאחר שאינן נבדלים מן העצם כלל, because really in the essence the essential idea of being kind is not like something that you learn and are taught, it's that you are kind, that God that part of being human means that you have this idea of kindness and empathy, that's an essential part of what it means to be you. שזהו ענין פרטי ממהות העצמות הפשוטה בתכלית, that this is just a certain aspect of the simple, transcendent essence of the soul. מכל מקום אי אפשר לומר בו שמתאחד במידת ניצוח ההיולית, and even though in a certain way you can describe it as just one aspect of the self, so seemingly then you could say, well, there's the aspect that's kind and the aspect that's that's of of נצח, of overcoming challenges and conquering things, but no, you can't describe them as being separate things that you unite with each other במידת נצח ההיולית הנטועה בעצם הנפש. You can't say that the attribute of kindness unites with this essential attribute of נצח the way it's implanted within the essence, מאחר שמיוחדים שניהם בעצמות, because they're both completely unified with the essence, ואינם נבדלים כלל כלל מן העצם, and they're not at all separate or distinct from the essence. And so, so now we started defining this type of relationship and the main metaphor we're using is this משל of the יחידה, the essence of the soul and how it relates to the other details, but it's a little difficult to appreciate how the the attributes of חסד and גבורה and נצח are really all the same to the essence of the soul. And so now we're going to give a second משל that's going to help us highlight that idea of how to the essence all of these different attributes are really one and the same. But for now let's just recap the basic idea. Again we're trying to give a משל to understand the relationship of the essence of the infinite light to the ten ספירות, to the attributes, and we say the משל for that is understanding our יחידה, which is God gives us the essence of our soul is just this simple ability of free choice, and the fact, and imprinted, part of the nature of what it means to be a human soul is that we have this ability of, let's say, curiosity, and empathy, and, you know, overcoming challenges, and all these kind of things. But all of those are really the same essence, and it's just different ways that that looks when you plug that same essence into the world. And so we can, we we kind of create these ways of dividing it up and discussing it, but that's kind of artificial. From the essence's point of view, it's really the same point. When you take that same idea of being human, and you plug that into, you know, one thing, it's going to look like curiosity. You plug it into something else, it's going to look like kindness. You plug it into something else, it's going to look like this type of idea of נצח, of of wanting to overcome challenges. And it's really just that same essential human quality that God has given us in our soul, and it's getting expressed and plugged into these different forms.
